label: National Energy Emergency Status
source: Office of the President, Executive Order 110
delta: In effect since March 24, 2026; Visayas hit a 4-hour red alert Sept 13 (yellow 4-5pm & 9-10pm, red 5-9pm; 2,109MW available vs 2,346MW peak demand) after Therma Visayas Units 1&2 and Panay Energy Development Corp Unit 3 went offline, with Visayas unable to import from Mindanao's own tight grid; Mindanao logged a yellow alert Sept 12 and 13 (5-7pm) as GNPower Kauswagan Units 2&3 (206MW) stayed down. 33 Visayas plants and 29 Mindanao plants remain on forced outage or derated. DOE's four-pronged plan (unit restorations through Oct 3, ~253MW of new battery storage across Cebu/Panay/Leyte/Negros, transmission fixes, generator accountability) still targets a stabilized Visayas grid by October. Fuel prices held near post-Sept 8 hike levels (national average ~₱92/L diesel, ~₱81/L gasoline as of Sept 13) after the big-time hike driven by Iran-US Strait of Hormuz tensions erased the Sept 1 rollback
